segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, so I pulled up the quote from the CRM. We have 48 seats for the operations package, annual term starting March 1, and the total comes to $38,400 before tax.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, that matches what I had. The only thing is we may need to add five warehouse supervisors in April. Can those be prorated, or do we need to amend the whole order?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: They can be prorated. We’d add them through a simple order form, same unit price, and the billing tool would calculate the remaining months on the term.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. And implementation, you had said four weeks. If we sign by February 12, are we still looking at go-live the week of March 18?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, that’s still workable. We’d do kickoff on February 19, data import by March 4, user training March 11 and 12, then go-live that following Monday.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Procurement asked about payment terms. Your quote says net 30, annual upfront. We can do annual upfront, but they’ll want the invoice dated after March 1.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: That’s fine. I’ll note invoice date March 1 in the order, and accounting can send it that morning. Due date would be March 31.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Also, our legal team had one comment on auto-renewal. They want 60 days’ notice instead of 30 if we’re going to cancel.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, that’s within our standard fallback. I’ll send that to deal desk, but it should be quick. No change to pricing or start date.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Send the updated order form and the contract redline today if you can. I’m trying to get signatures lined up before our Friday purchasing meeting.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. You’ll have the updated documents by 3 p.m. Central, and I’ll include a summary of the seat count, dates, and invoice timing in the email.
